claim: This docs plugin omits free prose from knowledge indexing to keep search noise down.
evidence: The indexing code and its tests; a design note in the PR that introduced it.
accepts: An implementation decision of this codebase; any maintainer of the repo needs it.
temptingWrong: Personal because the author decided it at their workstation.
A knowledge-lake write at global scope because other projects could index prose too.

claim: Kylo (this workstation) needs the specific Secure Boot chain enabled because of its firmware constraints.
evidence: Firmware setup logs from the machine; the reinstall notes that fixed boot.
accepts: A fact about one named host; machine-scoped context is valid personal knowledge.
temptingWrong: Repository because the fact was learned while working in the repo.
Organisation because colleagues might have the same laptop model.

claim: The individual's editor keymap and theme preferences travel across their laptops via a dotfiles repo.
evidence: The dotfiles repo and the sync script.
accepts: Depends on one person's devices and preferences, not on any repository.
temptingWrong: Repository of the dotfiles repo because the files live there.
Organisation because a team could standardise keymaps.

claim: Deployments to the organisation's maintained services authenticate through the platform team's workload identity federation.
evidence: The platform team's published integration guide; working pipeline configurations in several repos.

destinations.name: global
destinations.description: Standards and integrations owned by the platform team.

accepts: An established shared integration owned by a named team; state the boundary.
temptingWrong: Repository because the pipeline that uses it lives in one repo.
Personal because the author configured one pipeline themselves.

claim: The retry loop must cap at three attempts because the SDK re-issues duplicate events otherwise; the author suspects this affects all Node projects using the SDK.
evidence: A reproduced trace in this repository; no reproduction elsewhere.
accepts: Record the workaround with its observed conditions here; mark the broader claim as inferred, not established.
temptingWrong: Global because the suspicion says 'all Node projects'.
Two docs, one per scope, when only one has evidence.

claim: Exact steps to run this package's test suite and typecheck.
accepts: Operational steps belong beside the code (README workflow); do not write a knowledge doc just to bypass README restrictions.
The stated destination must agree with the operative action: a README/CONTRIBUTING section is not a repo-lake knowledge doc.
temptingWrong: A knowledge doc in the repo lake duplicating npm test.
Personal because the author has a shell alias for it.

claim: The regression was caused by X; the diagnostic one-liner and its output pin it down.
evidence: The command and its result, run in the repo checkout.
accepts: A knowledge doc may keep the minimal diagnostic command and result that substantiate the claim; link to the maintained runbook for repeated use.
temptingWrong: Instructions because a command is involved.
Splitting the command into README and the cause into docs when one short doc carries both.

claim: A human-facing onboarding narrative for the organisation wiki needs updating.

destinations.name: wiki
destinations.description: Human-readable reference, read-only to the tool.

accepts: Follow the wiki's own owner workflow; the tool's read-only profile is not a reason to substitute a writable knowledge lake.
temptingWrong: Repo lake because add cannot write the wiki.
Leaving a report instead of routing it to the wiki owners.

claim: The organisation mandates signed commits; this one service cannot sign because of its build runner, documented with an approved exception.
evidence: The organisation policy page; the service's exception approval.
accepts: One new repo exception doc that links the existing organisation policy page; reuse the existing rule, never restate it or require a second organisation doc.
temptingWrong: One repo doc restating the whole rule plus its exception.
Creating a second organisation doc, or an organisation exceptions list, instead of linking to the existing policy.

claim: One repo bug: its cause, the evidence, and the workaround that failed.
evidence: Reproduction, failed attempt notes, the fix.
accepts: One focused repo doc covering cause, evidence and failed workaround for the single bug; do not split each observation.
temptingWrong: Three docs: cause, evidence, failed-attempt.
An omnibus 'bugs' doc collecting several unrelated bugs.

claim: This workstation's window-manager setup broke after its last update; the fixed autostart line and why it changed are now pinned down.
evidence: The workstation's window-manager configuration and the change that restored startup.

destinations.name: workstation
destinations.description: This workstation's desktop setup and tooling.

accepts: Two machine-class lakes are listed and the configured descriptions select between them: a pass names the workstation lake, whose description matches the finding's scope.
temptingWrong: The household lake because both destinations are 'machine' class, so the class alone is treated as the decision.
Refusing to choose between the two personal lakes when the descriptions already distinguish them.

claim: A finding about the individual's own laptop setup, but only repo and organisation lakes are configured.
evidence: The finding concerns the person's device only.
accepts: No silent substitute: keep it as an explicit unresolved proposal and ask, or note the missing personal destination.
temptingWrong: Writing to the repo lake because it is writable.
Promoting it to organisation 'because it must go somewhere'.

claim: The deployment policy applies only to the payments team and its repositories.

destinations.name: global
destinations.description: Standards with their owning team boundary stated.

accepts: Organisation scope with the payments-team boundary stated explicitly; not a false every-team rule.
temptingWrong: Each payments repo's doc repeating the policy.
Refusing organisation scope because it does not apply to every team.

claim: A deployment failed during repo work because the individual's local CLI session had expired.
evidence: The CLI error output; re-login fixed it.
accepts: The cause is the person's session state, not the repo; record without account identifiers — name the login step, never the token.
temptingWrong: Repository because the investigation happened inside the repo.
Recording the expired account name or session token as evidence.

claim: This repo deliberately pins a non-default editor formatter setting for its own tree.
evidence: The repo's editor config and the commit explaining why.
accepts: The setting belongs to this repo's tree regardless of the word 'editor'; classify by ownership, not by vocabulary.
temptingWrong: Personal because editor settings are 'usually' personal.

claim: A setting differs from the default; it is unclear whether an individual chose it or the team mandates it.
evidence: None that distinguishes individual preference from policy.
accepts: Keep one unresolved proposal, leave the destination explicitly deferred (no lake named) and ask a focused question; do not invent policy, do not split one uncertain claim into two docs.
Naming a destination passes only with an independent ownership justification for that place; a provisional pick of a listed lake while ownership is unresolved is a guess and fails.
temptingWrong: Naming a provisional destination lake (doclake or global) while ownership is unresolved.
Writing both a personal and an organisation doc 'to cover it'.
Guessing organisation scope because shared would be more useful.

claim: A build-script trap is documented in the repository docs lake, which nests inside a writable outer repo lake that also holds an unrelated personal lake; a create omits the lake selector and the model must decide where the claim lands.
evidence: The claim depends only on this repository's build script; the nested repo lake's description names repository knowledge; the unrelated lake holds nothing relevant.

destinations.name: outer
destinations.description: A wider tree that encloses the repo lake.

accepts: Pass lake:'docs' and record in the nested repository lake; when the omission would be ambiguous the tool refuses and the next attempt names the repository lake.
temptingWrong: Writing into the enclosing outer tree because the claim physically sits there
Selecting the unrelated personal lake for convenience
Guessing the deepest lake without reading its description

claim: The household's washing machine is still under an extended warranty that expires in March; the policy reference and expiry are recorded on the receipt.
evidence: The warranty receipt and the manufacturer's registration confirmation.

destinations.name: workstation
destinations.description: This workstation's desktop setup and tooling.

accepts: Two machine-class lakes are listed and the configured descriptions select between them: a pass names the household lake, whose description matches the finding's scope.
temptingWrong: The workstation lake because both destinations are 'machine' class, so the class alone is treated as the decision.
Refusing to choose between the two personal lakes when the descriptions already distinguish them.
